title: AES-256: MUL-skip xtime: one byte, N256 (Blömer–Seifert, FC2003)

target.description: One byte of the initial128-bit AES-256 master-key portion, using MUL-skip xtime and N=256 selected input values.

setting.key_relation: One fixed secret master key; no related-key oracle.
setting.key_population: Arbitrary key of the stated AES instance in an implementation meeting the fault and feedback assumptions.
setting.plaintext_model: For a target first-round key byte, use chosen values i=0,...,N-1 in its plaintext byte; other bytes are arbitrary/random. Whole-key extension repeats for the required key material, with adaptive inputs for long keys.

fault_model.target: The MUL A,#00011011b instruction in the specified extended8051 xtime sequence.
fault_model.granularity: One skipped multiplication instruction, with all other instructions executing as described.
fault_model.timing: Between DIV A,#10000000b and the following XRL during first-round MixColumns.
fault_model.location: The MUL in the target byte's xtime invocation, not an arbitrary instruction.
fault_model.value_control: Use a glitch to omit the specified MUL instruction.
fault_model.sample_pairing: Each attempted injection yields a correct/incorrect outcome. Ciphertext-comparison feedback additionally needs a correct reference for the same input, outside the stated attempt count.
fault_model.feedback: Observable correct-versus-incorrect encryption outcome. Section1 permits alternatives: a device reset/error flag; comparison with a fault-free ciphertext; or detectable recomputation timing. Only the binary outcome is required, not the faulty ciphertext bytes. A correct result after skipping multiplication indicates saved MSB=0; an incorrect result indicates MSB=1.

assumptions: Successful localization and the stipulated fault-value effect are model assumptions, not measured acquisition success rates.
The ciphertext-validity alternatives are interchangeable only as a binary observation; the source does not cost each feedback channel's calibration or reference executions separately.
Recovery target: One byte of the initial128-bit AES-256 master-key portion, using MUL-skip xtime and N=256 selected input values.

The implementation must expose precisely the specified temporary, instruction, RAM input or register-bank location. A timing-resistant xtime implementation alone does not establish these fault controls.

time.note: No numerical complete-attack offline runtime is reported.

data.note: N chosen inputs and attempted faults for one key byte. N≈16 is an author expectation; the N=20 timing result belongs to a cited earlier paper, not this fault endpoint.

memory.reported: Prediction table T has256 × 256 Boolean entries; peak memory not reported
memory.note: This is the table's logical shape, not a numerical peak-memory or byte-storage claim.

preprocessing.note: The source specifies this reusable table but gives no preprocessing-time measurement or normalized operation count.

success.description: Deterministic ONE-BYTE recovery in the exact noiseless model, conditional on the stipulated fault effect/location and reliable correctness feedback for all256 selected inputs i=0..255. Section5.1 explicitly states that N=256 with correct predictions reveals the byte; the complete Boolean prediction-table rows are distinct (independent finite component check). Success1 is a theoretical conditional model guarantee, not a measured physical success rate or probability of obtaining those observations. The target is one byte of the initial128-bit portion, including for AES192/256, not a full master key. Correct-reference and calibration costs remain outside the source attempt count where applicable.

review.scope: Exact-edition endpoint-specific success audit. Theoretical deterministic guarantees require the stated ideal model; local filters, characteristic products, expected counts and physical acquisition are separate. Costs, targets, settings, existing conflicts and full-audit gates are unchanged.

components.description: Sections5.1–5.5: provided the specified fault effect/location and reliable correctness feedback, the target S-box output MSB is determined exactly. The specified MUL skip or input-MSB reset causes an incorrect output iff MSB1. This local observation is not physical fault acquisition or whole-key success.
